Pip sat on the green lawn.
Pip patted his paws.
Barnaby wagged his tail at the lawn.
Pip sat on a tree branch.
Pip held a small brown acorn in his paws.
"Woof!" Barnaby barked.
Pip scampered to the trunk along the branch.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip put the acorn on the soft dirt.
"The acorn is acorn number one," Pip chattered.
Pip scampered back up to the branch.
Pip grabbed another acorn from a leaf cluster.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip set the acorn near the small brown acorn.
"The acorn is acorn number two," Pip said.
Pip ran back to the branch up the trunk.
Pip picked a shiny brown acorn.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip put the shiny brown acorn.
Barnaby watched Pip collect the nuts.
Pip ran up the tree.
Pip grabbed a fat acorn from the twig.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip put the fat acorn in the line.
Pip climbed up the trunk.
Pip picked a smooth acorn from the branch.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip set the smooth acorn.
Pip scampered up the tree.
Pip picked a small acorn near a leaf.
Pip ran to the dirt down the trunk.
Pip put the small acorn in the row of acorns.
Pip ran to the branch up the trunk.
Pip grabbed a heavy acorn with his paws.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip put the heavy acorn.
Pip climbed back up to the branch.
Pip picked a round acorn from the cluster.
Pip ran to the dirt down the trunk.
Pip put the round acorn in the line.
Pip scampered up the trunk.
Pip picked a dark acorn from a twig.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip set the dark acorn.
Pip ran back up to the branch.
Pip picked a tiny acorn from the tree.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip put the tiny acorn on the dirt.
Pip climbed up the tree.
Pip picked a dry acorn near the top.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip put the dry acorn.
Pip picked a bright acorn from the branch.
Pip ran to the lawn down the trunk.
Pip set the bright acorn.
Barnaby looked at the row of the acorns.
"Twelve acorns!" Barnaby barked.
Pip buried all twelve acorns in the dirt.
Barnaby rested his chin on his paws.
"You left seven nuts on the lawn," Barnaby said.
Pip scampered over to the acorns.
Pip picked the small acorn up with his paws.
Pip ran to the wooden shed across the lawn.
Pip dug a small hole in the dirt.
Pip pushed the small acorn into the hole.
Pip covered the small acorn with a brown leaf.
Pip scampered back to the lawn.
Six acorns remained on the lawn.
Pip picked the heavy acorn up.
Pip ran to the garden fence across the lawn.
Pip dug a hole under a wooden post.
Pip pushed the heavy acorn into the dirt.
Pip covered the hole with fresh dirt.
Pip scampered back to the lawn.
Five acorns remained on the lawn.
Pip picked the round acorn up.
Pip ran over to the flowerbed.
Pip buried the round acorn under a purple flower.
Pip scampered back to the lawn.
Four acorns remained in the row of the acorns.
Pip picked the dark acorn up.
Pip ran to the big stone birdbath.
Pip buried the dark acorn in fresh dirt.
Pip scampered back to the lawn.
Three acorns remained on the lawn.
Pip picked the tiny acorn up.
Pip ran over to the compost box.
Pip buried the tiny acorn under two dry leaves.
Pip scampered back to the lawn.
Two acorns remained on the lawn.
Pip picked the dry acorn up.
Pip ran to the root of the tree.
Pip buried the dry acorn near the trunk.
Pip scampered back to the row of the acorns.
One acorn remained on the lawn.
Pip picked the bright acorn up.
Pip ran to the corner of the back yard.
Pip buried the bright acorn in fresh dirt.
Zero acorns remained on the lawn.
Pip sat on the lawn.
Pip patted his paws.
Barnaby wagged his tail at the lawn.
